output.summary: Hairless flowering perennial native in southern Britain only to counties including Somerset, Dorset and Hampshire, but distributed more widely through Europe, western Asia and North Africa. Its egg-shaped root tubers sit away from the stem base, and its fruiting heads are distinctively flat-topped; unlike other water-dropworts, it can occupy dry lowland habitats within its natural range. In Turkey, locals reportedly eat the tubers roasted, cooked with yoghurt and bulgur, or pickled and cooked in winter.
